speaker: Unknown
en: Every company on the planet has a celebrated persona.
zh: 地球上的每家公司都有一个备受推崇的人物形象。

speaker: Unknown
en: In a world where you believe that alpha comes from engineering and AI, you need to create a culture whereby the celebrated persona is the engineer, and that's what's required.
zh: 在一个你相信超额收益来自工程和 AI 的世界里,你需要打造一种文化,让备受推崇的人物形象是工程师,这就是必需的。

speaker: Unknown
en: You think about your typical investment in a fund, and you're typically trying to figure out how do we start to package to sell this thing in three years.
zh: 你想想你在一只基金里的典型投资,你通常是在琢磨我们如何在三年内开始打包并卖掉这个东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: That is just a very different framing for how we think about technological transformation and what are the investments you're willing to bring to bear here.
zh: 对于我们如何思考技术转型、以及你愿意投入什么样的投资,这只是一种非常不同的框架。

speaker: Unknown
en: What we do is scarce.
zh: 我们做的事情是稀缺的。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're trying to do one deal per year.
zh: 我们试图每年只做一笔交易。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's it.
zh: 仅此而已。

speaker: Unknown
en: Our job is to do one.
zh: 我们的工作就是做成一笔。

speaker: Unknown
en: Hi, listeners.
zh: 嗨,各位听众。

speaker: Unknown
en: Welcome back to KnowPriors.
zh: 欢迎回到 KnowPriors。

speaker: Unknown
en: Today, I'm here with Michael Lee, co-founder and CEO of Sequence Holdings.
zh: 今天,我和 Michael Lee 在一起,他是 Sequence Holdings 的联合创始人兼 CEO。

speaker: Unknown
en: They just announced the largest AI take private to date with the Dell family office of Baldwin for $7.7 billion.
zh: 他们刚刚宣布了迄今为止最大的 AI 私有化交易,与 Dell 家族办公室就 Baldwin 达成 77 亿美元的交易。

speaker: Unknown
en: We talk about this, the Sequence story, how AI transformation is actually going to permeate the economy and what transfers from public investing to private equity to operating.
zh: 我们会谈到这个、Sequence 的故事、AI 转型实际上将如何渗透到经济中,以及哪些东西从公开市场投资转移到私募股权再到实际经营。

speaker: Unknown
en: Welcome, Michael.
zh: 欢迎,Michael。

speaker: Unknown
en: Michael, thanks for doing this.
zh: Michael,谢谢你来做这期节目。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thanks for having me.
zh: 谢谢你们邀请我。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you started Sequence Holdings, which is a permanent holding company that works with management teams to buy and refund their businesses to be market leaders with AI.
zh: 所以你创办了 Sequence Holdings,这是一家永久控股公司,与管理团队合作,收购他们的业务并用 AI 重新注资,使其成为市场领导者。

speaker: Unknown
en: We should talk about that and it's a very exciting model, but you also announced this big transaction in Baldwin.
zh: 我们应该谈谈这个,这是一个非常令人兴奋的模式,但你们也在 Baldwin 上宣布了这笔大交易。

speaker: Unknown
en: Tell us about it.
zh: 跟我们讲讲吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, you know, we started the company 20 months ago really with an eye towards can we partner with world-class businesses and management teams working closely with our frontier engineering team to forge market leaders.
zh: 好的,你知道,我们在 20 个月前创办这家公司,真正的着眼点是:我们能否与世界一流的业务和管理团队合作,与我们的前沿工程团队紧密协作,打造市场领导者。

speaker: Unknown
en: The brokerage space is an area that we've been spending a lot of time on since the founding of the business.
zh: 经纪领域是我们自公司成立以来花了很多时间研究的领域。

speaker: Unknown
en: We've met dozens of insurance brokers, and Baldwin was truly N of one of all the insurance brokers that we've met.
zh: 我们见过几十家保险经纪公司,而 Baldwin 真的是我们见过的所有保险经纪公司中的唯一之选。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's been a privilege over the last few months to spend a lot of time with Trevor Baldwin and the management team, and we could not be more excited about the journey that lies ahead between us, the Baldwin team, and the Dell family office that supported us in this transaction.
zh: 在过去几个月里,能与 Trevor Baldwin 和管理团队共度大量时光是一种荣幸,对于摆在我们面前的旅程——我们、Baldwin 团队,以及在这笔交易中支持我们的 Dell 家族办公室——我们再兴奋不过了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want to zoom all the way out to a little bit about, you know, your background, you and your co-founder, Alex, how this idea for Sequence came about, because you've been, you know, an investor now, you know, a hybrid investor operator.
zh: 我想把视角拉得非常远,聊一点你的背景,你和你的联合创始人 Alex,Sequence 的这个想法是如何产生的,因为你现在一直是一名投资者,你知道,一种混合型的投资人兼运营者。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, tell me about how you arrived at the idea to begin with.
zh: 就是,跟我说说你最初是怎么想到这个主意的。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, when I first joined Lone Pine in 2017, one of the first areas that I was asked to cover was AI.
zh: 你知道,当我 2017 年刚加入 Lone Pine 时,我被要求覆盖的最早领域之一就是 AI。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's actually quite early.
zh: 那其实相当早。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was, you know, as I'm sure you recall, it's kind of when AlphaGo came out.
zh: 就是,我相信你记得,大概就是 AlphaGo 问世的时候。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's actually when the first Transformer paper came out.
zh: 其实也正是第一篇 Transformer 论文发表的时候。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there was a lot of excitement at the time around what would be commercially viable if you scale these architectures.
zh: 当时有很多兴奋的情绪,围绕着如果你扩展这些架构,什么会是商业上可行的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And at the time, these were convolutional neural nets, scans, LSTMs, and the like.
zh: 当时,这些是卷积神经网络、scans、LSTM 之类的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And, you know, I think we all know how the story ends, which is we obviously saw a lot of exciting things come out of it.
zh: 然后,你知道,我们都清楚这个故事如何收场,那就是我们显然看到了许多令人兴奋的东西从中产生。

speaker: Unknown
en: But as you scaled these architectures, there were degrading effects over time to scale.
zh: 但是当你扩展这些架构时,随着规模的扩大,随着时间的推移出现了性能退化的效应。

speaker: Unknown
en: I share that context because when the models came out or ChatGPT came out at the end of 22, what became obvious to me, at least, is that the world had forever changed.
zh: 我分享这些背景是因为,当这些模型问世或者说 ChatGPT 在 22 年底问世时,至少对我而言显而易见的是,世界已经永远改变了。

speaker: Unknown
en: We finally had an architecture that we knew could scale infinitely.
zh: 我们终于有了一个我们知道可以无限扩展的架构。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, whether or not that was possible, what would come from that was not clear, but we did know that we could scale with compute, that the architecture would improve.
zh: 当然,这是否可能、从中会产生什么,当时并不清楚,但我们确实知道我们可以随着算力扩展,架构会不断改进。

speaker: Unknown
en: And, you know, like an investor, I started to think about what were the impacts to the world.
zh: 然后,你知道,像一名投资者那样,我开始思考这对世界的影响。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I kind of felt strongly that AI would have an uneven impact on the economy.
zh: 我当时比较强烈地感觉到,AI 对经济的影响将是不均匀的。

speaker: Unknown
en: There are certain parts of the economy that I felt that AI just wouldn't impact at all, right?
zh: 经济中有某些部分,我觉得 AI 完全不会影响,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: Take restaurants, golf courses, things like that.
zh: 拿餐馆、高尔夫球场之类的东西来说。

speaker: Unknown
en: There are certain industries that I just felt like a startup would win.
zh: 也有一些行业,我就是觉得创业公司会赢。

speaker: Unknown
en: Take coding, for example, like Conviction and Sequence going to go buy and outsource coding services business feels like a terrible idea, which you will give money to Cognition or Toanthropic.
zh: 拿编程来说,比如 Conviction 和 Sequence 去收购外包编程服务业务,感觉是个糟糕的主意,你会把钱给 Cognition 或 Toanthropic。

speaker: Unknown
en: But as a student of business, there have always been certain industries where I felt like the incumbent had all the advantages.
zh: 但作为一个商业的学习者,一直存在某些行业,我觉得在位者拥有所有优势。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that could be brand, that could be scale, network effects, regulatory.
zh: 那可能是品牌,可能是规模、网络效应、监管。

speaker: Unknown
en: And in light of what is going to be the biggest technological shift of our lifetime, I felt very strongly that if you could acquire the right incumbent, inherit the advantages of being that incumbent.
zh: 而考虑到这将是我们此生最大的技术变革,我非常强烈地感觉到,如果你能收购正确的在位者,继承作为在位者的那些优势,

speaker: Unknown
en: Could you forge the market leader?
zh: 你能不能打造出市场领导者?

speaker: Unknown
en: And the kernel of that idea is the one that really is upon which Sequence was founded upon.
zh: 而这个想法的核心,正是 Sequence 得以创立的基础。

speaker: Unknown
en: Came up with the idea in early 23, had a handful of people try to get me to leave Lompon and go do it then.
zh: 我在 23 年初想出了这个主意,当时有几个人试图劝我离开 Lompon 去做这件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: Just wasn't the right time for me.
zh: 只是那时对我而言时机还不对。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then I remember going for a walk with my wife in 24, letting her know that, hey.
zh: 然后我记得在 24 年和我妻子散步，告诉她，嘿。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's pretty rare in life to be in the middle of the most important technological change of our lifetime.
zh: 人生中能身处我们这个时代最重要的技术变革之中，是非常罕见的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Having the kernel of an idea, I felt very strongly about and feeling very strongly that I could pull together the team to go and pull it off.
zh: 心中怀有一个我非常坚定的想法的雏形，并且非常强烈地感觉到我能够组建团队去把它实现。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so that's why we started Sequence and couldn't be more excited about kind of what we've been able to achieve to date and kind of what we see ahead of us.
zh: 所以这就是我们创立 Sequence 的原因，对于到目前为止我们所能取得的成就，以及我们看到的前方，我再兴奋不过了。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a super first principles approach to, you know, what is the macro change that is happening in technology?
zh: 这是一种非常第一性原理的方法，去思考正在技术中发生的宏观变化是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: How is it going to impact the economy?
zh: 它将如何影响经济？

speaker: Unknown
en: But, you know, many investors, at least venture investors would be like, oh, no, incumbents have a bunch of advantages.
zh: 但是，你知道吗，许多投资者，至少风险投资者会说，哦，不，在位者有很多优势。

speaker: Unknown
en: I guess it's just not for us.
zh: 我想这对我们来说不合适。

speaker: Unknown
en: How did you think about, you know, scale and the idea of being able to engage with or even own incumbents?
zh: 你是如何思考规模，以及能够参与甚至在位者、乃至拥有在位者这个想法的？

speaker: Unknown
en: That's a I guess you can just do things, but that's an ambitious premise.
zh: 那是——我想你可以就这么去做事情，但这是一个非常有雄心的前提。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's more just it's the.
zh: 我认为更多的是这是。

speaker: Unknown
en: Business model that meets the opportunity today.
zh: 契合当今机会的商业模式。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if we take a giant step back, at least at Sequence, when we think about what's happening with AI today, we think we're living through the equivalence of the next industrial revolution.
zh: 所以如果我们退一大步来看，至少在 Sequence，当我们思考今天 AI 正在发生什么时，我们认为我们正在经历相当于下一次工业革命的时期。

speaker: Unknown
en: And what we generally see in most enterprises, what I typically see from a lot of the software companies that are producing AI agents today, is this giant push to give small machines to every human in the human assembly line and to speed up work.
zh: 而我们在大多数企业中普遍看到的，也是我通常从许多正在生产 AI 智能体的软件公司那里看到的，是一种巨大的推动力，要给人类流水线上的每个人配上小机器，以加速工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there's nothing wrong with that.
zh: 这没有什么不对。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's great.
zh: 这很好。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's better than nothing.
zh: 总比没有好。

speaker: Unknown
en: But as you know, when you have machines that can work 24-7, that can scale with electricity, that can accomplish what no individual human or group of humans can do, the right answer is to think about how do you start to reorganize what an organization should be to meet the opportunity of what's available today with technology.
zh: 但正如你所知，当你拥有能够 24 小时 7 天工作的机器，能够随电力而扩展的机器，能够完成任何个人或人群都无法做到的事情的机器时，正确的答案是思考如何开始重组一个组织应该是什么样的，以迎接当今技术所带来的机会。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's the context upon which we're sitting in.
zh: 而这就是我们所处的背景。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think really in the first time, we have a real opportunity here to partner with amazing companies, with great leadership teams, partnering with our platform and our engineering team, and really thinking critically around how do we reorganize the organization?
zh: 而且我认为真的是第一次，我们有了一个真正的机会，可以与优秀的公司、出色的领导团队合作，与我们的平台和工程团队携手，并真正批判性地思考如何重组组织？

speaker: Unknown
en: How do we lean into what's best in terms of what the technology can do, what can humans do, and rethink how we can compete in these various industries?
zh: 我们如何充分利用技术能做到的最好的事情，人类能做什么，并重新思考我们如何在这些不同的行业中竞争？

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think it's just really more of an opportunity piece more so than an ambition piece in that, like, I just think this has to happen.
zh: 而且我认为这更多是一个机会的问题，而不是一个雄心的问题，因为，我只是觉得这必须发生。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I don't see it a natural way for it to happen unless you do it through our approach.
zh: 而且除非通过我们的方式去做，我看不出它有自然而然发生的途径。

speaker: Unknown
en: Can you talk a little bit about the structure of the company?
zh: 你能稍微谈谈这家公司的结构吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Like why a permanent holding company?
zh: 比如为什么是永久性控股公司？

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, what does ownership enable you to do that being a, you know, a vendor or a partner doesn't?
zh: 你知道，所有权能让你做到哪些作为供应商或合作伙伴做不到的事情？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I think there's two parts to that question.
zh: 是的，我认为这个问题有两个部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: So in terms of like the holding company structure itself, you know, when I thought about what is required to accomplish what Sequence Holdings wants to do.
zh: 所以就控股公司结构本身而言，你知道，当我思考要完成 Sequence Holdings 想做的事情需要什么时。

speaker: Unknown
en: Which is how do we partner with world-class organizations?
zh: 那就是我们如何与世界一流的组织合作？

speaker: Unknown
en: How do we bring frontier engineering to bear?
zh: 我们如何让前沿工程发挥作用？

speaker: Unknown
en: How do we build a platform that we can share across all of our portfolio companies?
zh: 我们如何构建一个可以在我们所有投资组合公司之间共享的平台？

speaker: Unknown
en: The only natural way to do this was through a holding company.
zh: 唯一自然的方式就是通过一家控股公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do we build a business whereby we can forge market leaders?
zh: 我们如何构建一门能够锻造市场领导者的生意？

speaker: Unknown
en: How do we align the duration of capital with the sustained investment and operational commitments that are going to be required to drive the transformation end to end?
zh: 我们如何使资本的期限与持续的投资和运营承诺相匹配，这些承诺是端到端推动转型所必需的？

speaker: Unknown
en: How do we create an organization that culturally is oriented around forging market leaders, not deploying capital?
zh: 我们如何创建一个在文化上围绕锻造市场领导者而非部署资本来定位的组织？

speaker: Unknown
en: And lastly, how do you create the right structure upon which you can take the retained earnings in your business to rethink about how do you support your existing companies and net new investments?
zh: 最后，你如何创建正确的结构，使你能够利用业务中的留存收益，重新思考如何支持你现有的公司和新的投资？

speaker: Unknown
en: And so when I think about the opportunities in front of us, the only natural way to go do this was through a holding company.
zh: 所以当我思考摆在我们面前的机会时，唯一自然的方式就是通过一家控股公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: In terms of your second question around ownership,
zh: 至于你的第二个问题，关于所有权，

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, let's maybe just play this out through an example.
zh: 你知道，也许我们可以通过一个例子来说明这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's say that you're an incredible business.
zh: 假设你是一个非常出色的企业。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I won't pick on one.
zh: 是的，我不会点名某一家。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's say we're a Fortune 500 company.
zh: 假设我们是一家财富 500 强公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have unlimited resources.
zh: 你拥有无限的资源。

speaker: Unknown
en: If I challenge you to say, hey, you're the CEO of this Fortune 500 company today and your job is to refund yourself, you're stuck with three options.
zh: 如果我向你挑战说，嘿，你今天是这家财富 500 强公司的 CEO，你的任务是重塑自己的公司，你只有三个选择。

speaker: Unknown
en: One is I'm going to go do it myself.
zh: 第一是我要自己去做。

speaker: Unknown
en: The structural challenge with that, and it's not a bad one, is just it's impossible to recruit and retain the talent required to go and do this refounding.
zh: 这样做的结构性挑战——这并不是一个糟糕的选择——只是，招募并留住完成这次重塑所需的人才是不可能的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the answer to that is actually much more obvious than people think, which is every company on the planet has a celebrated persona.
zh: 而这个问题的答案实际上比人们想象的要明显得多，那就是地球上的每一家公司都有一个备受赞誉的代表人物。

speaker: Unknown
en: So let's take Blackstone, for example, an incredible organization, one that I admire a lot.
zh: 以 Blackstone 为例，一个令人赞叹的组织，一个我非常钦佩的组织。

speaker: Unknown
en: And in fact, I make every person a sequence reading King of Capital.
zh: 事实上，我让 Sequence 的每个人都去读《King of Capital》。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the celebrated persona at Blackstone is the investor.
zh: 但在 Blackstone 备受赞誉的代表人物是投资者。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's why they're able to aggregate the greatest investors in the world.
zh: 这就是为什么他们能够聚集世界上最伟大的投资人。

speaker: Unknown
en: In a world where you believe that alpha comes from engineering and AI, you need to create a culture whereby the celebrated persona is the engineer.
zh: 在一个你认为 alpha 来自工程和 AI 的世界里,你需要创建一种文化,让被推崇的人物是工程师。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's what's required.
zh: 而这正是所需要的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's the reason why does Palantir exist?
zh: 这就是为什么 Palantir 会存在?

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm sure Alex Karp would hate how I would describe this, but it is foundationally an organization that has aggregated world-class engineers, that celebrates the engineer, and foundationally what they do is it's a wrapper to sell it to other organizations that are not able to get that talent.
zh: 我相信 Alex Karp 会讨厌我这样描述,但这在根本上是一个聚集了世界级工程师的组织,它推崇工程师,而他们从根本上所做的事就是一个 wrapper,把它卖给那些无法获得这种人才的其他组织。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that leads me to my second point.
zh: 所以这引出了我的第二点。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you can't get the talent to do it yourself, then there's this huge multi-trillion dollar industry that got formed called the services industry.
zh: 如果你自己无法获得人才,那么就有一个庞大的数万亿美元的产业形成了,叫做服务业。

speaker: Unknown
en: And these are great companies, Accenture, McKinsey, Palantir, that do celebrate the engineer, that do celebrate changing technology.
zh: 这些是伟大的公司,Accenture、McKinsey、Palantir,它们确实推崇工程师,确实推崇技术的变革。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the challenge that you have when you partner with a services provider in terms of rethinking and refounding your business is an incentives problem.
zh: 但当你与服务提供商合作来重新思考和重构你的业务时,你面临的挑战是一个激励问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: Services companies optimize for kind of three things, getting in your wallet, staying in your wallet, growing the share of your wallet.
zh: 服务公司优化的基本上是三件事:进入你的钱包、留在你的钱包里、扩大你钱包中的份额。

speaker: Unknown
en: It is a path towards incrementalism.
zh: 这是一条走向渐进主义的道路。

speaker: Unknown
en: To compound that, services providers can't actually change the things that you really need to really kind of meet the moment.
zh: 更糟的是,服务提供商实际上无法改变你真正需要改变的东西,才能真正跟上时代。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you change how the people are organized, who's working in these organizations, and the incentives?
zh: 你如何改变人员的组织方式、在这些组织中工作的人是谁,以及激励机制?

speaker: Unknown
en: And so if you can't do it yourself, you can't use vendors, and you have the third option, which is what a lot of people do, which is they go buy software.
zh: 所以如果你自己做不到,又不能用供应商,你就有第三个选择,也是很多人所做的,就是去买软件。

speaker: Unknown
en: The challenge with buying software is twofold.
zh: 购买软件的挑战有两个方面。

speaker: Unknown
en: The obvious one is that it's beta.
zh: 显而易见的一个是,它是 beta。

speaker: Unknown
en: If it's available to everybody, it's available to everybody.
zh: 如果它对每个人都可用,那它就对每个人都可用。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the part that's more nuanced that I think people often miss is that if you and I were starting a software company, the thing we would optimize for is what is a workflow that's reasonably homogenous that exists in a lot of places?
zh: 我认为更微妙、人们经常忽略的部分是,如果你和我要创办一家软件公司,我们会优化的是:什么样的工作流是相当同质的,并且存在于很多地方?

speaker: Unknown
en: And then how do we install it fast enough, but deeply enough, such that we can sell a lot, but it's sticky?
zh: 然后我们如何足够快地、但又足够深入地把它安装进去,这样我们既能卖很多,又有粘性?

speaker: Unknown
en: Those are the genetics- Structurally, yes, that sounds very attractive.
zh: 这些是基因——从结构上讲,是的,这听起来很有吸引力。

speaker: Unknown
en: That'd be the genetics of what we'd look for.
zh: 那会是我们寻找的东西的基因。

speaker: Unknown
en: What that means, though, is that you're always going to sell to a workflow as it's designed today, as the humans are set up in that human assembly line today.
zh: 但这意味着,你总是会按照今天设计的工作流来销售,按照今天人们在那条人类流水线上的设置来销售。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's the only way you can sell a product.
zh: 这是你能卖出产品的唯一方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can't sell a product around a new human assembly line that doesn't exist today because that's how you think it is.
zh: 你无法围绕一条今天还不存在的人类流水线来销售产品,即便你认为它应该是那样。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so when we think about why does our motion work, it's how do you have ownership so therefore you're aligned?
zh: 所以当我们思考为什么我们的模式能奏效时,就是:你如何拥有所有权,从而保持一致?

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you create an organization like Sequence Holdings that celebrates to engineer and bring frontier engineering to bear?
zh: 你如何创建一个像 Sequence Holdings 这样推崇工程师并让前沿工程发挥作用的组织?

speaker: Unknown
en: And then three, how do you drive a long-term horizon and economic model such that we're aligned with management around how do we think about how do we forge the best version of this company possible based on the technology that's available today?
zh: 然后第三,你如何推动一个长期视野和经济模型,使我们与管理层保持一致,共同思考如何基于当今可用的技术,打造这家公司可能的最佳版本?

speaker: Unknown
en: And so that's how we think about our business model.
zh: 这就是我们思考我们商业模式的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's why we think it works.
zh: 这就是为什么我们认为它能行。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the early evidence from kind of Bank South and kind of what we've observed in the field today have proven that out today.
zh: 来自 Bank South 的早期证据以及我们今天在现场观察到的情况,已经在今天证明了这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want to talk a little bit about Bank South as well, but you have a team that includes a bunch of like Scale and Palantir DNA.
zh: 我也想稍微谈谈 Bank South,但你的团队包含了大量 Scale 和 Palantir 的基因。

speaker: Unknown
en: You are trying to keep the quality bar really high.
zh: 你试图把质量标准保持得非常高。

speaker: Unknown
en: What is compelling to the team, the engineers that work at Sequence?
zh: 对团队、对在 Sequence 工作的工程师来说,什么是有吸引力的?

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's a bunch of things.
zh: 我认为有很多方面。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the first is really it's an opportunity to kind of work on the companies that actually are the capillaries upon which people interact with.
zh: 我认为第一个是,有机会去研究那些真正是人们与之互动的毛细血管的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, the AI model companies are phenomenal.
zh: 你知道,AI 模型公司非常了不起。

speaker: Unknown
en: We would not be here today if it weren't for Anthropic, OpenAI, xAI, and the like.
zh: 如果没有 Anthropic、OpenAI、xAI 之类的公司,我们今天不会坐在这里。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the reality is like the impact to everybody's day-to-day lives really are going to be impacted by the companies that serve them today.
zh: 但现实是,对每个人日常生活的影响,真正会来自那些今天服务他们的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so for us, it's the opportunity to partner with really important companies that play an important role in the economy and really thinking about how do we bring world-class technology to bear to deliver differentiated experiences for their customers.
zh: 所以对我们来说,这是与在经济中扮演重要角色的真正重要的公司合作的机会,并真正思考如何让世界级的技术发挥作用,为它们的客户交付差异化的体验。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that mission is like quite powerful.
zh: 我认为这个使命相当有力量。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think, you know, when I think broadly about the two engineering personas that we typically hire from, I think, you know, call it the four deployed engineers, I think that the thing that appeals to them is the opportunity to be really aligned with the value that they create.
zh: 你知道,当我宽泛地思考我们通常招聘的两种工程师画像时——姑且称之为那四位部署工程师——我认为吸引他们的,是真正与他们所创造的价值保持一致的机会。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that's an extremely rewarding experience.
zh: 我认为那是一种极其有回报的体验。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think the ability to drive the type of change that would not be possible if you were a service provider is quite appealing.
zh: 而且我认为,能够推动那种如果你是服务提供商就不可能实现的变革,是相当有吸引力的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the other hand, which is probably not as fun for venture capitalists to think about, is like, you know, when I talk to application software engineers, it's, hey, we're one of the few business models in the world that's completely immune to what the model is going to do.
zh: 我认为另一方面——这对风险投资人来说可能不那么有趣——是,你知道,当我和应用软件工程师交谈时,他们会说:嘿,我们是世界上为数不多的、对模型将要做的事完全免疫的商业模式之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: As the model performances improve, we celebrate here at Sequence, and that gives us more tools to bring to bear in the companies that we partner with.
zh: 随着模型表现的提升,我们在 Sequence 这里为之庆祝,这给了我们更多的工具,可以带到我们合作的公司中去发挥作用。

speaker: Unknown
en: And like there's no real existential risk to whether or not our business will be around.
zh: 而且我们的业务是否还会存在,并没有真正的生存风险。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think those are kind of things that have appealed.
zh: 我认为这些就是有吸引力的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the mission is probably the thing that drives it at the end of the day, but I do think there are tangibles when we talk with candidates that have been quite appealing for kind of what we're trying to build.
zh: 我认为归根结底,使命可能是驱动一切的东西,但我确实认为,当我们与候选人交谈时,有一些切实的东西,对我们正在努力构建的目标来说是相当有吸引力的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I remember when you first told me, hey, we think we're gonna go buy a piece of a bank and partner with the Bank South team.
zh: 我记得当你第一次告诉我,嘿,我们打算去买一家银行的一部分股权,并与 Bank South 团队合作。

speaker: Unknown
en: I might've reacted with some mild horror about the difficulty and regulatory concerns around that.
zh: 我当时可能对此表现出了一些轻微的惊恐,关于这件事的难度和监管方面的担忧。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I was like, Michael, you must know that
zh: 我当时就说，Michael，你一定知道

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a reason that banking is not a popular private equity sector traditionally.
zh: 银行业传统上不是私募股权的热门领域，这是有原因的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Tell us a little bit about how you chose financial services and then what you've learned in the BankSouth partnership so far.
zh: 请跟我们讲讲你是怎么选择金融服务的，以及到目前为止你在 BankSouth 合作中学到了什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, you know, I think it's worthwhile to take a step back and thinking about how did this investment come to be?
zh: 那么，你知道，我觉得值得退一步想想，这项投资是怎么来的？

speaker: Unknown
en: And then kind of maybe to tackle kind of how and why it's been kind of the perfect place for us to start our business.
zh: 然后再大概谈谈，为什么、以及怎么，它会成为我们创业起步的完美起点。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, you know, when we started this business, call it March of last year, when you first kind of wrote the first investment, the sequence, you know, we had a cold start problem, right?
zh: 你知道，当我们创办这家公司时——大概是去年 3 月，当你写下第一笔投资、那个 sequence 的时候，我们面临一个冷启动问题，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: So the holding company models a weird business.
zh: 控股公司模式是个很奇怪的生意。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like without money, you can't do a deal.
zh: 没有钱，你就做不了交易。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you don't have a deal, you can't hire engineers.
zh: 没有交易，你就雇不到工程师。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you can't hire engineers, anyone wants to give you money.
zh: 雇不到工程师，就没人愿意给你钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thankfully, you were willing to support us.
zh: 所幸你愿意支持我们。

speaker: Unknown
en: We were able to get a handful of engineers to come work with us, but yet we were stuck with kind of the cold start problem of nothing really to do.
zh: 我们得以招到几个工程师加入我们，但我们还是卡在冷启动问题上——没什么真正可做的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: And one of the things that we were debating at the time was, do we just go buy something to prove to the world that we can buy something and change it, or do we wait for the right asset?
zh: 我们当时争论的一件事是：我们是随便买点东西向世界证明我们能买东西并且改造它，还是等一个合适的资产？

speaker: Unknown
en: And as I think you know, we've always had a bias towards scale and enterprise.
zh: 正如我想你知道的，我们一直偏爱规模化和企业级。

speaker: Unknown
en: Unfortunately, there are not a lot of investors in the world that want to give you hundreds of millions of dollars to buy an enterprise to see whether or not your technology works.
zh: 遗憾的是，世界上没有多少投资人愿意给你几亿美元去买一家企业，来看看你的技术到底行不行。

speaker: Unknown
en: So what we decided to do is to go and take on a customer.
zh: 所以我们决定去做的是去找一个客户。

speaker: Unknown
en: And, you know, we called a dear friend, Jamie Reynolds.
zh: 然后，我们给一位挚友 Jamie Reynolds 打了电话。

speaker: Unknown
en: He's one of the co-founders of Avenir.
zh: 他是 Avenir 的联合创始人之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: And basically framed for him, hey, like, here's the problem that I've run into.
zh: 基本上就是跟他说：嘿，我遇到了这样一个问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And very fortunately, his family happens to own a bank down in Georgia.
zh: 非常幸运的是，他家正好在佐治亚州拥有一家银行。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's how it became our first customer.
zh: 于是它就成了我们的第一个客户。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that started off August of last year.
zh: 那是去年 8 月开始的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: In fact, it was August 4th.
zh: 事实上，是 8 月 4 日。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was my anniversary.
zh: 那是我的结婚纪念日。

speaker: Unknown
en: I remember skipping it.
zh: 我记得我跳过了它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it was an incredible experience.
zh: 那是一段非常棒的经历。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so from August to about November, like kind of late November of last year, basically operated in a services motion and like really started to tackle kind of the key workflows that existed at the bank.
zh: 所以从 8 月到大约去年 11 月底，我们基本上以服务模式运作，真正开始着手解决那家银行存在的关键工作流。

speaker: Unknown
en: Fortune to us, you know, the family asked us at that point in time whether or not we'd become a permanent partner.
zh: 对我们来说幸运的是，那家人在那时问我们愿不愿意成为长期合作伙伴。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's how it became our first investment.
zh: 于是它就成了我们的第一笔投资。

speaker: Unknown
en: We ended up closing the investment in March, took us a little while to kind of negotiate everything as well as get Fed and OCC approval.
zh: 我们最终在 3 月完成了那笔投资，花了些时间谈判所有事宜，以及获得美联储和 OCC 的批准。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I think it's, I share all that context to say that like operating in a services motion and then being an investor, we saw a night and day difference.
zh: 但我想，我分享这些背景是想说，以服务模式运作和作为投资人，我们看到了天壤之别。

speaker: Unknown
en: Right?
zh: 对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a lot of things.
zh: 这体现在很多事情上。

speaker: Unknown
en: One is from an engineering perspective, you know you're going to be here for a long time.
zh: 其一是从工程角度看，你知道你会在这里待很长时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the level of complexity and depth that you're willing to take on versus being a service provider, knowing that you'll eventually leave and have to leave behind applications that other people have to maintain is demonstrably different.
zh: 所以你愿意承担的复杂度和深度，与作为服务提供者——知道你终将离开、不得不留下需要别人维护的应用程序——相比，有着显著的差别。

speaker: Unknown
en: The second thing is just a lot of excitement from the employee base around, hey, these people are here to support us for a long time.
zh: 第二件事是员工群体中有很多兴奋感，围绕：嘿，这些人是来长期支持我们的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So how do we push the most ambitious version of this?
zh: 那么我们怎么把它推向最雄心勃勃的版本？

speaker: Unknown
en: And then three is like, really, we can take a long-term orientation around like, what do we want this bank to look like three years, five years, 10 years from now?
zh: 然后第三是，真的，我们可以采取长期导向，比如，我们希望这家银行在三年、五年、十年后是什么样子？

speaker: Unknown
en: And how do we lay the technological foundation such that we're always benefiting from model performance?
zh: 以及我们如何打下技术基础，使得我们始终能从模型性能中受益？

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's what we've been able to do.
zh: 这就是我们一直以来能够做到的。

speaker: Unknown
en: In a weird way, the bank was the perfect pilot for what we need to do to validate our business model.
zh: 说来也怪，这家银行是我们验证商业模式所需的完美试点。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was an ability to buy into minority stakes, so a venture-scale type check, to operate in a real enterprise-like environment.
zh: 它让我们能够买入少数股权，也就是一笔风险投资规模的支票，在一个真正类企业的环境中运作。

speaker: Unknown
en: And in a weird way, the regulated nature of the bank was a feature, not a bug.
zh: 而且说来也怪，银行受监管的性质是一个特性，而不是缺陷。

speaker: Unknown
en: One of the nice things about a regulated institution is that how it operates is well-defined.
zh: 受监管机构的好处之一是，它的运作方式是明确定义的。

speaker: Unknown
en: The data hygiene is excellent.
zh: 数据卫生非常出色。

speaker: Unknown
en: There are well-defined rules around how your business is supposed to operate.
zh: 围绕业务应该如何运作，有着明确定义的规则。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so if you think about that context, it actually works extremely well for agents.
zh: 所以如果你想想那样的环境，它实际上对智能体极其有效。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's one piece.
zh: 这是一方面。

speaker: Unknown
en: The other piece that's really important for banking, which has been quite a learning for us in terms of how we think about investing, is the centralized nature of it.
zh: 另一个对银行业非常关键的方面——这也给我们思考投资方式带来了很大的启发——是它的集中化性质。

speaker: Unknown
en: So when we talk at Sequence about companies we're looking for, we talk a lot about organizational physics.
zh: 所以当我们在 Sequence 谈论我们在寻找什么样的公司时，我们经常谈到组织物理学。

speaker: Unknown
en: We like organizations that are quite dense and the operations are centralized.
zh: 我们喜欢非常紧凑、运营集中化的组织。

speaker: Unknown
en: So anything you build can be amortized over a large base.
zh: 这样你构建的任何东西都可以摊销到一个庞大的基础之上。

speaker: Unknown
en: So like take a bank, for example.
zh: 比如拿一家银行来举例。

speaker: Unknown
en: A bank may have a bunch of different branches, but all the underwriting happens centrally.
zh: 一家银行可能有很多不同的分支机构，但所有的承保都是集中进行的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So everything we build at headquarters gets amortized over all the branches that they're working with.
zh: 所以我们在总部构建的一切，都可以摊销到他们所服务的所有分支机构上。

speaker: Unknown
en: You contrast that with, I think, a lot of the roll-ups that we see out in the marketplace today, which I think is an awesome strategy, but there's a lot of complexity with it.
zh: 与之形成对比的是，我认为，如今市场上看到的很多整合收购(roll-up)策略，我认为这是一个很棒的策略，但它有很多复杂性。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have to integrate different systems.
zh: 你必须整合不同的系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have to send engineers to a number of different places.
zh: 你必须把工程师派往许多不同的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have to standardize operating procedures.
zh: 你必须标准化操作流程。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have to standardize cultures.
zh: 你必须标准化文化。

speaker: Unknown
en: And for us, the nice thing about the bank is that while it's a large organization with $100 million plus of sales, the physics of the business are quite dense.
zh: 而对我们来说，银行的好处在于，虽然它是一个销售额超过一亿美元的大型组织，但这个业务的物理学是非常紧凑的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And therefore, we've been able to make a lot of progress in a short period of time.
zh: 因此，我们能够在很短的时间内取得很大的进展。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a central nervous system.
zh: 有一个中枢神经系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a ledger.
zh: 有一本总账。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's some key processes.
zh: 有一些关键流程。

speaker: Unknown
en: There are levers you can pull economically.
zh: 有一些可以在经济上拉动的杠杆。

speaker: Unknown
en: Exactly right.
zh: 完全正确。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why insurance brokerage?
zh: 为什么选择保险经纪？

speaker: Unknown
en: So the brokerage space has been an area that we've been spending a lot of time in since the founding of Seacoins.
zh: 从 Seacoins 创立以来，经纪领域一直是我们花大量时间研究的领域。

speaker: Unknown
en: It fits a lot of the things that we look for.
zh: 它符合我们寻找的很多条件。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so what do we look for broadly when we're as an organization?
zh: 那么作为一个组织，我们广泛地在寻找什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: We think about one is scale of the market.
zh: 我们考虑的第一点是市场规模。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, what we do here at Sequence doesn't scale.
zh: 你知道，我们在 Sequence 做的事情是不具备规模化的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if we're going to make an investment, we need it to count.
zh: 所以如果我们要做一笔投资，就必须让它算数。

speaker: Unknown
en: We want to work on companies that we think we can build into $100 billion plus companies.
zh: 我们想做的就是那些我们认为可以打造成一千亿美元以上公司的业务。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like you're not going to do this 10 times a year.
zh: 因为你不可能一年做十次这种事。

speaker: Unknown
en: No, we're not an investment shop.
zh: 不，我们不是一家投资店铺。

speaker: Unknown
en: We partner with great companies to force leaders.
zh: 我们与优秀的公司合作，成为行业领导者。

speaker: Unknown
en: The second thing that we cared a lot about is, is it an industry where the incumbent has all the advantages?
zh: 我们非常关心的第二点是，这是不是一个在位者拥有所有优势的行业？

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'm happy to go into that in greater detail.
zh: 我很乐意更详细地展开讲这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then three is, if we think about what the organization does and what AI is good at today, and we think about the overall app.
zh: 第三点是，如果我们思考这个组织在做什么、以及 AI 如今擅长什么，再思考整体的应用。

speaker: Unknown
en: Can we build something special?
zh: 我们能不能构建出一些特别的东西？

speaker: Unknown
en: And the broker's industry in a lot of ways fits all of that.
zh: 而经纪行业在很多方面都符合所有这些条件。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a $2 trillion plus of premiums per year going to carriers.

zh: 自从我们介入这家银行以来，我们花了大量时间的，是如何不仅改善承保，还如何确保组织中所有人都专注于他们最擅长的事情？
